answer: An island timber council uses a quill to log a daily simultaneous 30-minute muster in one hall. Each booth holds one person bound to one key. Two stewards sign a day/booth/key receipt after continuous attendance. Verifiers check both signatures and allow one vote per booth and key daily. No receipt means no vote. n active keys need n bodies and 0.5n person-hours daily; one person cannot staff two booths. Proxies can be hired, and colluding stewards can forge receipts. It limits votes per body, not coordinated control.
